text:
alex: Heads up — after the kernel-selector v3 rollout we see a consistent p99 tail during short bursts. Pattern looks like: burst arrives -> microbatching doesn't fill -> KV cache misses -> kernel fallback to slow-path -> autoscaler scales but with ~30s lag -> long tails (~1.5–2s). p95 sits ~110–150ms. p99 spikes to ~1.8s in experiments. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/ops/latency?run=slowhandshake :eyes:

maya: Ugh. Is this only in the 2–4x QPS bursts or also a steady-state throughput?

alex: Mostly the 2–6s surge windows. Steady-state is fine. I profiled a canary run and attached the hot spots (snippet below).

alex: ```
sample 1: kernel_choice.select_variant 34%
sample 2: kv_cache.lookup 18%
sample 3: memcpy/transpose 12%
fallback path (int8->fp16 conv) 9%
context switch / scheduling 6%
```

sanjay: Interesting that kernel_choice is top. That suggests the selector is doing expensive checks per request under low batch fill. Maybe the heuristics expect larger batch sizes. What are our microbatch parameters?

alex: Current runtime config (canary):
```
continuous_batching: true
min_batch_fill: 2
max_batch_wait_ms: 12
microbatch_target_tokens: 64
prober.sample_window_s: 10
prober.scale_decision_threshold: 0.25
runway_preheat: enabled
kv_prewarm_ttl_s: 0  # default, cold on burst
```

dmitri: Two quick things to try: 1) bump min_batch_fill to 4 and max_batch_wait_ms to 18 to reduce per-request kernel selection churn; 2) prober should pre-warm KV for low-latency kernels — set kv_prewarm_ttl_s to at least 60 for the first 2 min after a burst is detected.

carla: This smells like a regression from the v3 selector that added fine-grained architecture checks. We flipped to more aggressive fallbacks when batch < 4. Can we 1) add hysteresis to kernel fallback (only fallback after 2 consecutive misses) and 2) avoid recomputing selector on every microbatch if the shape/token-length is unchanged?

maya: +1 to hysteresis. Also let's capture a microtrace around the kernel handoff so we can see cost of selection vs execution. Short traces (100–200ms) will show selector overhead if it's happening synchronously.

alex: Running a two-arm controlled experiment now: A = selector_v3 + small batch adjustments, B = selector_v2 + kv_prewarm. Goal: p99 < 500ms during 2–6s bursts while preserving 95th throughput. I'll post results in ~40m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment triggered for experiment A (selector_v3 tweaks) and B (selector_v2 + kv-prewarm). Canary ids: c-4421 / c-4422.

sanjay: Also consider moving some expensive checks to async post-accept path (i.e., don't block first token). For most models the initial kernel can be optimistic. If we mispredict, let fallback happen during tokens 2–4 instead of blocking the entire request. Might reduce initial tail.

dmitri: I prototyped an optimistic_fastpath earlier — it reduced median by ~8ms but cut p99 in half for microburst sims. Worth trying as a short patch.

carla: Important: keep telemetry for these dimensions in the rollout (kernel_variant, batch_fill, kv_hit, scale_event_id). Without that we won't know which arm is winning during complex bursts.

maya: Also add a synthetic test in perf suite: short spike generator (QPS 0->200 for 6s) with both cold and warm KV states. That should reproduce.

alex: Results update (20m): A shows p99 median 980ms (still bad), B shows p99 median 420ms (better) but throughput dips 6% under heavy sustained load. Raw numbers:
- baseline steady: p95 120ms, p99 220ms
- burst A: p95 150ms, p99 980ms
- burst B: p95 160ms, p99 420ms, throughput -6%

alex: Tradeoff: selector_v2 + kv-prewarm wins tail but costs throughput. Need to find sweet spot for SLOs vs unit cost.

sanjay: If we can keep p99 < 500ms by kv prewarm + slight microbatch increase, I think it's acceptable even with -5–7% throughput. Products expect stable tail.

dmitri: We should also test adaptive policies: when a burst is detected, temporarily relax throughput-optimized kernels and favor low-latency variants for X seconds, then revert. Combine with runway_preheat to hide scale-up lag.

carla: Agree. Also document the risk: too aggressive low-latency variants increase GPU time per token -> higher unit cost. Need cost dashboard by kernel variant.

maya: OK next steps: 1) merge kv_prewarm TTL=60 to canary, 2) add selector hysteresis, 3) perf test for spike generator, 4) enable kernel telemetry. I'll own 1+3. Sanjay owns 2. Dmitri will run the optimistic_fastpath A/B. Carla will add cost breakdown.

alex: Thanks — I'll watch canaries and post final numbers. If B remains better for tails we'll roll it but gate with a cost alert. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary c-4421 succeeded, c-4422 failed smoke (fallback to baseline). Rolling back c-4422.

alex: Noted. c-4422 failing explains B's instability under sustained load. Will iterate on kv_prewarm logic and re-run.

maya: Nice work team. Pinging @carla @sanjay for telemetry schema review before full rollout. :eyes:

carla: On it. Will add fields and a compact tracing span for kernel selection.

sanjay: I'll push the hysteresis patch in an hour and schedule the perf job.

alex: Great. Closing loop later with final numbers.
